patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff is an unrelated GOST documentation merge and does not touch lib/x509/pkcs12.c. The authoritative clean fixed image also reaches `_decode_pkcs12_auth_safe` with the same 5-byte initialized prefix for `oid`, so the fixed-side cleanliness is not evidence of a source-level repair to the missing initialization obligation.

nodes.description: At the `strcmp(oid, DATA_OID)` sink, the compare span implied by `sizeof(DATA_OID)` is 21 bytes while only the first 5 bytes of `oid` are initialized in the witnessed vulnerable execution.
nodes.evidence: Vulnerable assertion trace shows oid_strcmp.cmp_bytes=21 and oid_strcmp.oid_initialized_prefix_len=5.

edges.description: The same stack buffer `oid` filled by `asn1_read_value(..., oid, &len)` is the buffer passed unchanged into the subsequent `strcmp` sink.
edges.evidence: Vulnerable assertion trace shows oid_read.oid_buffer == oid_strcmp.oid_buffer (same stack address).

root_cause_criterion.description: After `asn1_read_value(pkcs12, "authSafe.contentType", oid, &len)` succeeds, the bytes of `oid` that the upcoming `strcmp(oid, DATA_OID)` may consume must already be initialized. In the vulnerable execution only the `0.32\0` prefix is initialized, leaving the remainder of the 21-byte compare region indeterminate.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable assertion trace violates the required predicate (5 initialized bytes < 21 compare bytes). The authoritative fixed image is clean but still reaches the same source-level state (5 initialized bytes < 21 source-level compare bytes); its cleanliness comes from a different compiled sink implementation (`__interceptor_strcmp` instead of the vulnerable fixed-width memcmp expansion), so the required assertion is not differentially verified by the staged fixed assets.
